title: When I was a child
summary: Stem + te after the letters of 't kofschip, else + de; plural + n: werkte(n), speelde(n). leven → leefde. Stems in t or d double: praatte, antwoordde. Irregular: was/waren, had/hadden.
explain:
The simple past (*de onvoltooid verleden tijd*, often just *de o.v.t.*) is the tense for **what things were like** in the past, for **habits** and things that happened again and again, and for **telling a story**. It is one word: `Als kind speelde ik veel buiten`. It often goes with `vroeger` (in the past, "used to"), `toen` (then, at that time), `als kind`, `altijd` and `elke zomer`.

### The form: stem + te or de

Take the stem, as in the present tense. Then use the same rule as for the participle (unit A2 · 13): after a letter of **'t kofschip** (t, k, f, s, ch, p) add `te`, after any other letter add `de`. In the plural add an extra `n`.

| | werken | spelen |
| ik, jij / je, u, hij, zij | werkte | speelde |
| wij, jullie, zij / ze | werkten | speelden |

There are only two forms: one for the singular and one for the plural. Jij gets no extra t: `Werkte jij?`, `jij werkte`.

> Mijn vader werkte in een fabriek. — My father worked in a factory.
> Wij speelden elke middag voetbal. — We played football every afternoon.
> Woonde jij vroeger ook in de stad? — Did you also use to live in the city?

The spelling of the stem is the same as in the present: `maken → maakte`, `horen → hoorde`, `stoppen → stopte`.

### v and z: look at the infinitive

As with the participle, the rule looks at the stem **before** v becomes f and z becomes s. V and z are not in 't kofschip, so you add `de`: `leven → leefde`, `reizen → reisde`, `verhuizen → verhuisde`.

> In 2010 verhuisden we naar Utrecht. — In 2010 we moved to Utrecht.

### Stems in t or d: a double letter

Here, unlike the participle, nothing is dropped. A stem in t gets `te`, a stem in d gets `de`, and you write the letter twice: `praten → praatte`, `wachten → wachtte`, `antwoorden → antwoordde`, `landen → landde`.

> De juf praatte veel over haar kat. — The teacher talked a lot about her cat.

Careful: `wij praatten` (past) sounds exactly like `wij praten` (present). Only the spelling and the context tell them apart.

### Word order and separable verbs

The past form is the conjugated verb, so it stands in second place, or first in a yes/no question. A separable verb splits, as in the present: `Ik belde hem op`, `Ik groeide op in Odesa`.

> Vroeger haalde mijn oma mij van school op. — My grandmother used to pick me up from school.

### was and had

Two irregular verbs you need from the start:

| | zijn | hebben |
| ik, jij / je, u, hij, zij | was | had |
| wij, jullie, zij / ze | waren | hadden |

> Mijn eerste juf was erg streng. — My first teacher was very strict.
> We hadden vroeger een hond. — We used to have a dog.

Strong verbs, such as `ging`, `kwam` and `zag`, have their own past forms (unit A2 · 16). Do not give them a regular ending: *ik loopte is wrong.

### Watch out

- 't kofschip: `werkte`, not *werkde; `speelde`, not *speelte.
- v and z: `leefde`, not *leefte; `verhuisde`, not *verhuiste.
- Stem in t or d: `praatte`, `wachtte`, `antwoordde`, not *praate or *antwoorde.
- The plural needs its n: `wij speelden`, not *wij speelde.
- A separable verb splits: `Ik belde haar op`, not *Ik opbelde haar.

### Compared with Ukrainian

The Ukrainian past changes for gender (`я грав`, `я грала`). The Dutch past changes only for number: `ik speelde`, `wij speelden`, for a man and a woman alike. A Ukrainian imperfective past for a habit, `щоліта я їздила до бабусі`, is very often a Dutch simple past with a time word like `elke zomer`.

words.en: to do crafts / to make things

sentences.nl: Als kind speelde ik elke dag buiten.
sentences.en: As a child I played outside every day.
sentences.note: The stem speel ends in l, not a letter of 't kofschip, so + de: speelde. Als kind comes first, so the verb comes before ik.
alt: Ik speelde als kind elke dag buiten.

sentences.nl: Vroeger woonden we in een klein dorp.
sentences.en: We used to live in a small village.
sentences.note: English "used to" is the Dutch simple past, often with vroeger. Woon + de, and + n for the plural: woonden.
alt: We woonden vroeger in een klein dorp.

sentences.nl: Mijn oudere broer plaagde mij altijd.
sentences.en: My older brother always teased me.
sentences.note: plagen → stem plaag, ending in g: + de, plaagde. A habit in the past is a typical use of the simple past.
alt: Mijn oudere broer plaagde me altijd.

sentences.nl: Op het schoolplein wachtten we op de juf.
sentences.en: We waited for the teacher in the school playground.
sentences.note: The stem wacht ends in t, so + te gives a double t, and the plural adds n: wachtten. It sounds like the present wachten.
alt: We wachtten op het schoolplein op de juf.

sentences.nl: Toen verhuisden we naar een andere stad.
sentences.en: Then we moved to another town.
sentences.note: The stem of verhuizen ends in z in the infinitive, so + de: verhuisde, plural verhuisden. Ver- is part of the verb and stays.
alt: We verhuisden toen naar een andere stad.

sentences.en: Did you also use to collect stickers?
sentences.note: The singular form verzamelde is the same for jij, with nothing added or dropped when jij follows it.

sentences.nl: In mijn jeugd had ik weinig speelgoed.
sentences.en: In my childhood I had few toys.
sentences.note: hebben is irregular in the past: ik had, wij hadden. In mijn jeugd stands first, so had comes before ik.
alt: Ik had in mijn jeugd weinig speelgoed.

sentences.nl: Elke zomer logeerde ik bij mijn tante.
sentences.en: Every summer I stayed with my aunt.
sentences.note: logeren → stem logeer (the long e is written double), ending in r: + de. Elke zomer marks a repeated action.
alt: Ik logeerde elke zomer bij mijn tante.

sentences.nl: Mijn klasgenoten waren altijd heel aardig.
sentences.en: My classmates were always very nice.
sentences.note: zijn is irregular: was in the singular, waren in the plural. Mijn klasgenoten is plural: waren.

sentences.nl: Ik groeide op in een groot gezin.
sentences.en: I grew up in a big family.
sentences.note: opgroeien is separable and splits in the simple past too: groeide … op. The phrase in een groot gezin may follow op or come before it.
alt: Ik groeide in een groot gezin op.

exercises.note: The stem straf ends in f, a letter of 't kofschip, so + te. De meester is singular: strafte, not straften.

exercises.en: As children we played outside a lot.
exercises.note: The stem speel ends in l, so + de, and we needs the plural n: speelden. Speelten mixes up 't kofschip.
Look at the infinitive leven: the stem ends in v, not f. V is not in 't kofschip, so + de: leefde.

exercises.nl: Als kind ___ ik elke ochtend op de bus.
exercises.en: As a child I waited for the bus every morning.
exercises.note: The stem wacht already ends in t, and + te makes the t double: wachtte. Wachtten is the plural.

exercises.nl: De juf ___ (praten) veel over haar hond.
exercises.en: The teacher talked a lot about her dog.
exercises.note: praten → stem praat, + te: praatte, with a double t. Praate does not exist.

exercises.nl: Ik ___ (verstoppen) me altijd achter de deur.
exercises.en: I always hid behind the door.
exercises.note: The stem verstop ends in p, a letter of 't kofschip: + te. Ver- is part of the verb, and the stem has one p.
The z of verhuizen counts, so + de, and mijn ouders is plural: verhuisden. Not verhuisten.

exercises.en: We used to have a dog.
exercises.note: hebben is irregular in the past: had in the singular, hadden in the plural.

exercises.en: My first teacher was very kind.
exercises.note: The past of zijn is was in the singular and waren in the plural. Mijn eerste juf is singular.

exercises.en: Our teacher always answered very calmly.
exercises.note: The stem antwoord ends in d, so + de gives a double d: antwoordde. Every letter is written.

answers: Vroeger verzamelde ik altijd oude munten.
exercises.en: I always used to collect old coins.
exercises.note: Vroeger takes the first place, so the verb comes second and ik follows it.

answers: Mijn moeder haalde mij elke dag van school op.
Mijn moeder haalde mij elke dag op van school.
exercises.en: My mother picked me up from school every day.
exercises.note: ophalen splits in the simple past: haalde stands second, op goes towards the end. Van school may come before or after op.

exercises.task: Put it in the simple past.
exercises.from: Op woensdagmiddag knutselen we met de juf.
answers: Op woensdagmiddag knutselden we met de juf.
exercises.en: On Wednesday afternoons we did crafts with the teacher.
exercises.note: The stem knutsel ends in l, not a letter of 't kofschip, so + de, and we needs the plural n: knutselden.

exercises.task: Put it in the simple past.
exercises.from: Hij belt zijn moeder elke avond op.
answers: Hij belde zijn moeder elke avond op.
exercises.en: He called his mother every evening.
exercises.note: opbellen splits in the past as in the present: belde … op. The stem bel ends in l, so + de.

exercises.wrong: Wij speelde vaak op het schoolplein.
answers: Wij speelden vaak op het schoolplein.
exercises.en: We often played in the school playground.
exercises.note: Wij is plural, so the past form needs an n: speelden.

exercises.wrong: Op de kleuterschool huilte ik elke ochtend.
answers: Op de kleuterschool huilde ik elke ochtend.
exercises.en: At nursery school I cried every morning.
exercises.note: The stem huil ends in l, which is not in 't kofschip, so + de: huilde.
